summary:
The defect is repaired in the parallel rows for the part that belongs to them, and it is not the whole of what the two models show. Branch stage1-parallel-scale, three commits on fa8430e24, head 5b87457a5; 482 tests pass in both builds (473 before); nothing pushed.

What exists now. Of two parallel rows the one with the larger coefficients is kept and the smaller index only between rows of one size, so the removed row is the kept one times a ratio of at most 1. The image of a side is exact wherever it is a double. Sides that cross are measured in the units of the removed row. Rows that are parallel only within tol.zero are merged, and an equation is subtracted from such a row, only when they differ by at most a tenth of the tolerance over the bounds of their columns. Two options switch the kept row and that limit.

What was verified. Model 1 (zero-cost singleton rule after the merge) is a test that fails on the base with 1.5625e-3 and passes now, in both orders of the rows. On the 240 and the 17 local dumps, default and primal-only, nonzeros, rows and columns equal the base on every instance; the reduced-model hash differs on momentum1 and rocII-5-11 only; no merge is refused. Campaign of the committed tree: 113.0 million release and 47.5 million assertion models, clean except one failure that the base commit shares (below). 92 of 104 wrong engines are caught by a campaign check, the 90 of the 99 old ones as before.

What you must know before relying on it.
1. Model 2 (the doubleton substitution) is NOT closed, and cannot be closed in the parallel rows: the row of 2^18 alone, without any parallel row, fails by the same 1.563e-3 at the base commit. The doubleton substitution shifts a side by 2.36e13 with no limit on the size. It is not a test, because it fails.
2. Model 1 with all rules on (default options) also still fails by 1.563e-3, in both engines and both orders, and again without any parallel row: the free singleton column on an inequality restores its column at 9e7 with the rounding of a double, which a row with coefficients of 2^18 reads as 1.6e-3.
3. The oracle cannot reach this class: inside its class every later step is exact on integer data, and a column at a third of 9e7 misses a row of 2^20 in the oracle's own points. The wrong engine that keeps the smaller index is therefore caught only by a new verdict (sides) on a new profile of models outside the oracle class (scale_pair), on the second model and on 5.4% of that profile's models; oracle and structure check do not see it.
4. A new failure of the base commit, not of classes (a) to (c): assertion campaign with --singletons, profile default (and scaled), seed 31150507986, variant 6: the structure check fails alone in its postsolve part. The base fails it identically in both builds. Not repaired.

Not done: the doubleton and free-singleton defects above, the solver verdicts, the node, the 44 testbed instances, solution quality, HISTORY.md and ASSUMPTIONS.md entries (task rules).
design:
Checked against the code before building, as asked. The design documents of Stage 1c do not prescribe the kept row. One citation of the task differs from the code: alias_scale_limit (include/gprs/rules.hpp:409, 1e6) limits simple probing and the lock alias only; the alias of a doubleton equation has no limit on its scale or its offset.

Your reading holds for the kept row and I built it: larger coefficients kept, read from the coefficient of the smallest core column; smaller index when the two sizes are equal exactly. Four things in merge() did not survive the exchange of roles and were changed.

1. Image of a side. The old form, side / rounded ratio, is off the exact value by a rounding unit when the kept row is 3 or 1000003 times the removed one, and that reads as a crossing of two sides that meet. Now: side times kept coefficient over removed coefficient, with the error of the product carried into the quotient, on mantissas so that no size of coefficient overflows. Exact wherever the result is a double; the side itself between rows of one size, so pairs of ratio 1 and -1 give what they gave.

2. Unit of the crossing test. With roles exchanged the old test measures in the units of the larger row and reports infeasible where the smaller row holds within its tolerance at the side of the larger. With the old roles it accepted a crossing within the tolerance of the smaller kept row and left the larger row off by the ratio (0.524 at 2^20: a second model that fails on the base, now a test). Now the crossing times |ratio| is measured, which is what the removed row is off by; the new side is the opposite side of the kept row.

3. Rounding of the image. A rounded image is used only when the side of the removed row is at most feasibility / side_error (1e8); the error allowance of a rounded image (8 rounding units) and the drift are added and taken off in the crossing test, and a crossing that they do not place on one side of the tolerance leaves the pair alone. An image that is not finite leaves the pair alone.

4. Rows parallel only within tol.zero. Not bounded by any guard at the base: x0 + x1 <= 0 and x0 + (1 + 9e-10) x1 <= 0 over bounds of 1e7 leave the removed row off by 9e-3 (third model that fails on the base, now a test). Now the differences of the coefficients are read without rounding from two exact products, times max(|lower|, |upper|) of their columns, and must stay within options_t::parallel_drift_share (0.1) of the tolerance. Exact multiples pass over any bounds; a difference next to a column without a bound refuses.

Classes of three or more rows: each row goes into the first larger row it meets and that row can go in turn; every ratio is at most 1, so the product is. keeps_sides is now asked of the larger row; a pair whose larger row holds a fixed term above 1e8 is left where the base merged it when the smaller row came first (none on the 240 and the 17).

Refusals that read column bounds or the fixed terms of the kept row report limited, because both change without an event of the pair (a second presolve would otherwise change a fixed point).

Item 3, the subtraction of an equation. The ratio class does not exist there: the rule already asks |factor| <= 1, and 1 next to a singleton column of the equation. The class of point 4 does exist there (probe subtract_drift.cpp: 9.0e-3 on base and on my first commit). The repair is the same limit and certain, so I made it (second commit).

Deviations from the task. (a) Model 2 is reported, not a test. (b) The campaign reaches the class through a profile outside the oracle class with a verdict of its own, not through a knob judged by the oracle; the in-class knob exists as well. (c) I changed two tests in tests/test_engine_fixed_point.cpp and one in tests/test_e2e_presolve.cpp, whose scenarios rested on the smaller index being kept; each still tests what its name says. (d) Commit trailers: git commit -s put a second Signed-off-by after the Co-Authored-By line; I rewrote the two messages with git commit-tree and moved my branch with git reset --soft (trees unchanged), so the tested tree 6f0eb9a3 is that of 5d7147611. The third commit carries the sign-off line in its text.

- pr_fixed_roles (fixed terms of the two rows exchanged in the image): oracle 1,222, structure 442; 32 unit tests.
- pr_cross_kept, pr_no_drift, pr_sub_no_drift: one unit test each, no campaign check (the generated rows are exact multiples and no crossing is below one unit of the smaller row).

Check tool without a solver (gprs_check built against the committed release library). 240 local dumps, both modes per dump: 240 results, 5,040 verdicts pass, 4,320 skipped (solver), 0 failed; kept rows tested 10,727,053 in default mode (235,429 through a parallel record) and 11,452,469 in primal-only mode. 17 local dumps, default and primal-only: 34 results, 980 pass, 352 skipped, 0 failed.

Second presolve on real instances: all 234 fixed-point results of the 240 in default mode and 233 in primal-only mode return unchanged; all 17 of the 17 in both modes.

Models for items 3 and 4 (scratch probe/, each with no parallel row unless said):
- dbl_large.cpp, doubleton substitution: one row 2^18 (y + z) in [2^18 * 0.1, 2^18 * 5.3] and y - v = 9e7. Base: postsolved point violates the row by 1.563e-3. No named limit bounds the shift.

- Forcing column: no model found; my model B is reduced by other rules before the rule sees it.

reductions:
Instance sets: the 240 local dumps and the 17 local dumps, default and primal-only mode, committed binary, against the stored base results (results/bench240/s1c_m1_mac) and a run of the base binary on the 17.

Against the engine before (the base): nonzeros, rows and columns are equal on every one of the 240 instances in both modes and on every one of the 17. Sums on the 240: 101,227,465 nonzeros, 10,472,693 rows, 9,674,821 columns in default mode; 104,903,223 / 11,189,001 / 10,147,207 in primal-only mode. Status, fixed-point flag (234 and 233 of 240; 17 of 17), rounds of merges (351,049 and 352,085) and subtractions (8,916 and 8,924) are equal as well. No instance differs in a size, so there is none to explain, and no guard refused a merge or a subtraction on either set. options_t::parallel_drift_share = inf gives the same results on both sets.

Where a merge changed its kept row: two instances of the 240, in both modes, none of the 17.
- momentum1: 1,229 merges keep the row with the larger index. At the base those rows were removed into rows up to 794,000 times smaller (smallest new ratio 1.26e-6); their sides are 0 there.
- rocII-5-11: 14 merges, ratios of 1.05 to 1.15.
The reduced-model hash and the stack hash differ on exactly these two instances and on no other. With options_t::parallel_keep_larger off the reduced-model hash equals the stored base on all 240 and all 17.

Against the HiGHS reference m1_a, default mode (analysis/bench240_stage1c.py): geometric mean of reference over engine 1.0020 / 1.0022 / 1.0022 in nonzeros / rows / columns on the 237 and on all 240, the figures of milestone M1. Below 0.95: irish-electricity, rows 0.9352 and columns 0.8944, as at the base; its cause is the growth limit of the free singleton column (M1), not this change. Nonzeros: none below 0.95. Primal-only against m1_a: 0.9540 / 0.9616 / 0.9340 on the 237, as at the base. The other references (m1_b, m2_a, d3_cheap and so on) were not run; with equal sizes on every instance their figures are those of the base.

Total 9.1388 s against 9.2254 s (+0.9%). Parallel rows 0.9748 s against 0.9944 s (+2.0%, 0.020 s over 240 instances). Parts that I did not touch moved between -3.4% (finish) and +4.3% (storage), state +2.5%, so the total is inside the noise of this run and the +2.0% of the family is not resolved from it. Campaign speed: 25 million release models of one profile in 132 to 157 s on three processes; 21 million over all profiles in 90 to 175 s.

assumptions.title: Which of two parallel rows is kept
assumptions.statement: The row with the larger coefficients is kept and the other is removed, so that the removed row is the kept one times a ratio of at most 1 in size. Between rows of one size the smaller index is kept.
assumptions.alternatives: The smaller index whatever the sizes (the base); a limit on the ratio; a reach factor per row that every later rule guards with.
assumptions.measured: Off: reduced-model hash equal to the base on all 240 and all 17 local dumps. On: hash differs on momentum1 (1,229 merges) and rocII-5-11 (14), sizes on none. Off as a wrong engine (pr_keep_index): 6,462 failed side-point results in 1,680,000 campaign models, 5.4% of the scale_pair models.

assumptions.title: How the size of a row is read
assumptions.statement: The sizes of two parallel rows are compared by the absolute coefficient of the smallest core column, and equal means equal as doubles. Rows parallel within tol.zero can then have a ratio up to 1 + 1e-9 on another entry.
assumptions.alternatives: Largest coefficient of the row; a norm; equal within a tolerance.

assumptions.title: Arithmetic of the image of a side
assumptions.statement: The side of the removed row becomes side times kept coefficient over removed coefficient, with the error of the product carried into the quotient, computed on mantissas: exact where the result is a double, the side itself between rows of one size.
assumptions.alternatives: Side divided by the rounded ratio (the base), which is off an integer by a rounding unit for a ratio such as 1/3.
assumptions.measured: With the kept row unchanged (option off) the reduced-model hash equals the base on all 240 and 17 local dumps, so the new arithmetic changed no side there. Not compared on random models.

assumptions.title: Unit in which crossing sides are measured
assumptions.statement: Two sides that cross are infeasible when the crossing times |ratio| is above the feasibility tolerance, which is what the removed row is off by when the kept row holds at its side; otherwise the new side is the opposite side of the kept row. A pair that is infeasible in exact arithmetic by up to tolerance / |ratio| in the units of the kept row is therefore merged, not reported infeasible.
assumptions.alternatives: Units of the kept row (infeasible sooner, as the base did when the larger row came first); leave such a pair alone.
assumptions.measured: Unit test parallel_crossing_in_the_units_of_the_removed_row; the wrong engine pr_cross_kept fails it and no campaign check. No such crossing on the 240 or 17 local dumps (no merge count changed).

assumptions.title: Rounded image only at a size that holds the tolerance
assumptions.statement: An image that is rounded (the side less the fixed terms, the scaling or the sum with the fixed terms of the kept row is not exact) is used only when the side of the removed row, less its fixed terms, is at most feasibility / side_error (1e8). An exact image has no limit on its size. An image that is not finite, or a side below 2^-960 other than zero, leaves the pair alone.
assumptions.switch: tolerances_t::side_error = 1e-14 and tolerances_t::feasibility (shared with the other size guards); min_scaled_side = 2^-960 is a named constant without a switch
assumptions.alternatives: No limit (the base); the limit on the image in the units of the kept row, which would refuse a side of 100 next to a ratio of 2^20.
assumptions.measured: Refuses no merge on the 240 and the 17 local dumps (no side of a removed row is above 1e8 there). Other values not measured.

assumptions.title: Error allowance of a rounded image
assumptions.statement: A rounded image is taken as off by up to 8 rounding units of its size or of the fixed terms of the kept row. The allowance is added and taken off in the crossing test; a crossing that it and the drift do not place on one side of the tolerance leaves the pair alone.
assumptions.alternatives: No allowance (the base: a crossing of 1.004e-6 can be closed as 0.999e-6 next to a fixed term of 5e7); a larger band.
assumptions.measured: Unit test parallel_crossing_next_to_the_tolerance. Other values not measured.

assumptions.title: Limit on rows that are no exact multiples (merge)
assumptions.statement: Rows that are parallel within tol.zero and not exactly are merged only when the removed row differs from its multiple of the kept row by at most parallel_drift_share of the feasibility tolerance over the explicit bounds of the core columns: the sum of the coefficient differences, read without rounding from two exact products, times max(|lower|, |upper|). A difference next to a column without a finite bound refuses.
assumptions.switch: options_t::parallel_drift_share = 0.1; gprs_presolve --parallel-drift-share <x>, inf for no limit
assumptions.alternatives: No limit (the base); a limit that forgives differences of a rounding unit next to unbounded columns; implied bounds in place of explicit ones.
assumptions.measured: inf gives identical results on the 240 and the 17 local dumps: no merge is refused at 0.1. 152 merges on momentum1 are no exact multiples at the base; their drift is 2.2e-16. Other sets not measured: rows from decimal data such as 0.1 and 0.3 next to unbounded columns would be refused.

assumptions.title: The same limit for the subtraction of an equation
assumptions.statement: An equation is subtracted from a row with a parallel core only when the target differs from the factor times the equation by at most the same share over the bounds of the core columns.
assumptions.switch: options_t::parallel_drift_share = 0.1 (the same option as the merge)
assumptions.alternatives: No limit (the base); a share of its own.
assumptions.measured: Subtractions on the 240 local dumps: 8,916 default and 8,924 primal-only, equal to the base; 564 on the 17. No subtraction refused. Model subtract_drift.cpp: 9.0e-3 without the limit.

assumptions.title: Bounds that the drift reads
assumptions.statement: The drift is taken over the explicit bounds of the columns at the time of the merge; implied bounds that are kept apart do not count, and a column with an infinite explicit bound refuses a pair with a difference in that column.
assumptions.alternatives: Implied bounds; a nominal value for an infinite bound.

assumptions.title: Refusals that report limited
assumptions.statement: A pair left for the drift, for a crossing inside the band, or for a rounded image whose only rounding is that of the fixed terms of the kept row reports limited, so the presolve does not claim a fixed point: bounds and plainly absorbed fixed terms change without an event of the pair. A pair left for an image that is not finite, or for a rounded image at a size above the limit for another reason, does not.
assumptions.alternatives: List the rows of a column whose bound moves for the parallel rows (cost: every bound change); report limited for every refusal.
assumptions.measured: Fixed-point flags on the 240 local dumps: 234 default, 233 primal-only, as at the base; 17 of 17 on the local dumps. Campaign: 0 changed second presolves in 13.9 million.

assumptions.title: The guard on the fixed terms now reads the larger row
assumptions.statement: keeps_sides (fixed terms of the kept row at most feasibility / side_error) is asked of the larger row. A pair whose larger row holds a larger fixed term is left alone, also where the base merged it because the smaller row had the smaller index.
assumptions.alternatives: Fall back to the smaller row as the kept one (not valid: the class of this task).
assumptions.measured: No merge lost on the 240 and the 17 local dumps. Unit test parallel_huge_fixed_terms has one such pair.

assumptions.title: Generator knob and the two campaign profiles
assumptions.statement: p_parallel_scale gives a parallel row or its source one integer row factor from 2 to 2^20 (half powers of two, half from a fixed list of other integers), at most one per row. Profile parallel_scale uses it with p_parallel_row 0.5, p_scaled 0, p_equation 0.3, p_ranged_row 0.3. Profile scale_pair makes fixed-shape models outside the oracle class (ranged rows only, tenths as sides, ranges up to 9e7, one multiple in five negative) and is judged by the verdict sides alone.
assumptions.switch: generator_options_t::p_parallel_scale = 0, max_parallel_scale_exp2 = 20; gprs_fuzz --profile parallel_scale / scale_pair. The constants inside scale_pair_case have no switch.
assumptions.alternatives: Equations and one-sided rows in scale_pair (both make the right engine fail through the doubleton and free-singleton defects and through dual fixing with a term that cannot be absorbed); the verdict sides on every profile.
assumptions.measured: scale_pair: zero_cost_singleton fires on about 21% of the models; the wrong engine pr_keep_index fails 5.4% of them. The verdict sides was not tried on the other profiles.

not_done: Model 2 is not closed and is not a test. The doubleton substitution shifts the sides of the rows of the substituted column by coefficient times offset with no limit on the size: 2.36e13 in a row of 2^18, rounded to 0.004. The row of 2^18 alone fails by 1.563e-3 at the base commit (probe dbl_large.cpp, variant 1). A repair belongs in the admissibility of an alias (every row of the child takes the shift at a size that holds the tolerance, for the composed map as well) and needs a limited report or an event, since a coefficient of the column can change without listing the equation. I did not build it: the task says report for the alias, and milestone M2 is moving that code.

Model 1 under default options still fails by 1.563e-3 in both engines: the free singleton column on an inequality restores its column from a row with terms of 2.4e13 (probe single_row.cpp, no parallel row). Not repaired; it is the singleton-column family of milestone M1. A fix would limit the size of the terms of the pivot row, or round the restored value of a column on an inequality towards the side that holds.
Alias scale with the implied-bound band of the free singleton column (probe other_places.cpp, model A): bound passed by 1.0e-4 in primal-only mode. Reported, not repaired.
Forcing column: no model found; only reasoning (its undo takes a minimum of quotients, each with the rounding of the restored value times the coefficient of its row).

The base failure found by the assertion campaign (structure check alone, part postsolve, --singletons, profile default and scaled, seed 31150507986, variant 6) is not repaired. It is none of the known classes (a) to (c).

No identity run on random models between the engine with both options off and the base engine. With the kept row switched off the extra pass over a row still costs work units, so budgets can stop a call elsewhere; identity holds on the 240 and 17 local dumps in the reduced-model hash.
The wrong engines pr_cross_kept, pr_no_drift and pr_sub_no_drift are caught by one unit test each and by no campaign check.
The verdict sides runs on the profile scale_pair only; it was not tried on the other profiles.

Nothing was run with a solver (the solver verdicts of the check tool are skipped: 4,320 on the 240, 352 on the 17). Nothing ran on the node or on the 44 testbed instances. Solution quality was not measured for any assumption.
The other HiGHS references (m1_b, m2_a, m2_b, m3_a, d3_nine_a, d3_cheap, highs_cheap_all) were not rerun; only m1_a.
No HISTORY.md entry and no ASSUMPTIONS.md entry (task rules: no .md documents, no writes into the gpu-presolve worktree). Not pushed.

Tolerance used by several merges in a row (a row closed onto a kept row that is later closed onto a third) can add up to more than one tolerance for the first row. That exists at the base for rows of ratio 1 and I did not change it.
unsure: Whether you want the crossing measured in the units of the removed row. It keeps the contract (kept row exact, removed row within its tolerance) and agrees with the base for ratios of 1 and -1, but it merges a pair that exact arithmetic calls infeasible by up to tolerance / |ratio| in the units of the kept row. The campaign cannot tell the two choices apart.

The cost of the drift limit outside these two sets. It refuses nothing on the 240 and the 17, but rows written from decimal data (0.1 and 0.3) are no exact multiples as doubles, and next to a column without a bound such a pair is now left. I did not measure another set.

The error allowance of 8 rounding units and the claim that the two images of one row never change their order rest on my analysis of the arithmetic, not on a proof. The ordering is an assertion and held on 47.5 million assertion models.
The timing: +0.9% in total and +2.0% in the family were measured under a load average of 8 to 12, with untouched parts moving by up to 4.3%. I cannot say from this run whether the family got slower.
Why the unit tests of the old wrong engine m_parallel_tight end in a crash with the new code (the table marks it). The campaign catches it (11,786 oracle failures) and I did not look further.

My reading that the oracle cannot reach the class at all inside its class rests on the argument in the summary and on one experiment (the wrong engine passes 1.68 million models of all in-class profiles, parallel_scale included, with 0 oracle and 0 structure failures). A generator with sides of many bits might still reach it; I did not try one.
The new base failure: I traced it to a saved side of 5.55e-17 in a forcing record, but did not establish which of the two, the undo or the replay of the check, should give way.

The campaign has 14 profiles: models are seeds per profile times 14. The profile scale_pair ignores the profile options (--singletons is skipped for it, --columns does nothing); a new option such as --probing must skip it too. All its models count as 'base outside the oracle class' by design.

A profile that sets p_parallel_scale must keep p_scaled at 0: with both a row can be 2^30 times its base row, where the oracle's own point for a third of a small integer misses the row by more than 1e-6.

Trap for the shared substitution code of M2: an alias shifts the sides of the rows of the substituted column with no limit on coefficient times offset (probe dbl_large.cpp). Simple probing aliases go through the same code, with offsets as large as the bounds of the column. The profile scale_pair has no equation for this reason.

Trap in the singleton-column rules: the undo of a free singleton column rounds the restored value at its own size, which a pivot row with large coefficients reads times the coefficient (probe single_row.cpp, 1.563e-3 at the base). The guard reads the sides of the row, not its terms.
